frequency_question: How often have major central banks activated or raised their countercyclical capital buffer from zero during non-crisis economic expansions within a comparable 3-year structural window?
membership_rule: Members are established post-2010 Basel III implementations where the countercyclical buffer was maintained at 0% during baseline conditions; excluded are initial transitional phases or emerging market regimes without fully developed macroprudential frameworks.

cases.name: Bank of England CCyB active deployment cycle
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation
Swiss National Bank / Federal Department of Finance countercyclical buffer reactivation
Federal Reserve Board CCyB setting check window

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier
coverage_note: 4 named hits out of approximately 10 relevant peer central bank observations maintaining active frameworks.
known_gaps: Varying statutory thresholds and differing domestic mandates between the Federal Reserve and foreign central banks regarding intermediate financial stability indicators.
skeleton: Total advanced economies with structural CCyB frameworks evaluated over rolling 3-year windows where economic conditions permit activation.
multiplier: 4 successful formal regulatory activations across major jurisdictions / 10 major systemic banking jurisdictions operating the framework continuously over comparable windows
validity_reason: The baseline operational habits of post-crisis macroprudential committees remain stable until major structural rewrites of international Basel frameworks occur.
